title: Agent-Populated Simulated First Job for Juniors
one_liner: A 12-week simulated first job where new grads work inside a persistent fake company staffed by AI coworkers, clients and managers, producing an auditable work record employers trust.
customer: Employers pay $4-8k per hire or subscribe to pre-screened cohorts. Universities and bootcamps pay per-seat licences ($500-1,500), and state workforce boards fund seats. Start with RevOps, FP&A or customer-success analyst roles.
problem: The bottom rung is gone. Employers don't hire juniors because AI absorbs the tasks they learned on, and internships or apprenticeships need employer bandwidth, the very thing missing. Grads can't get the experience employers demand (Stanford: 19% gap, 42% underemployment).
solution: A persistent multi-agent world with a messy CRM or ledger, a ticket queue, stakeholder agents with hidden goals who change requirements, an AI manager giving 1:1s and an on-call incident. The junior works with their own AI tools and everything is logged. Senior humans grade a few deliverables weekly. The output is a portable 'experience ledger' (hours, artifacts, review outcomes, error-detection rates) employers can inspect.
why_now: Long-horizon agent capability and multi-agent simulation now make believable coworkers affordable (Project Vend-style and TheAgentCompany-style experiments), employers say they can't evaluate candidates in AI-permitted interviews, and the freeze is widening.
revenue_model: Employer per-hire success fees and pre-screen subscriptions, university licences and modest learner fees.
non_obvious_insight: The cold start of apprenticeship marketplaces is employer supply. A simulation removes it: the employer is fake but the evaluation is real. Employers hire on traces of judgment rather than resumes, and the moat is a scenario library built from anonymised real incidents.
first_30_days: Build one role sim (RevOps analyst) with 4 agent personas. Run it with 20 recent grads via a college career centre. Get 5 mid-size SaaS employers to review the graduates' traces and commit to interviews.

title: Interim Smoke-Damage Protocol Before the State Standard
one_liner: Publish and run the defensible smoke, ash and soot assessment protocol that California insurers, adjusters and lawyers will need on January 1, 2027, because the official technical standard will not exist until 2028-2029.
customer: California carriers, the FAIR Plan and their TPAs (for AB 1795's 30-day inspection and testing obligations), plus public adjusters, policyholder attorneys, and escrow, lender and buyer parties in standing-home sales. Homeowners pay via their insurer, PA or directly.
problem: California signed AB 1795 and AB 1642 on Sept 15, 2026. From Jan 1, 2027, insurers must inspect within 30 days, pay for necessary testing, keep paying ALE until restoration, and face a presumption that ash, soot and char in a standing home are fire-caused. But the state toxics department will not finish lead and asbestos standards until end of 2028 and other contaminant standards until 2029. Meanwhile tens of thousands of claims will need a protocol that survives litigation; existing vendor assessments are already accused of being substandard, and capacity of qualified industrial hygienists is scarce and expensive.
solution: An independent, openly published interim assessment protocol built on existing standards (IICRC S700, established sampling and lab methods, EPA/HUD dust-wipe criteria), developed with certified industrial hygienists and a toxicologist. Delivered as a product: a sampling-plan generator (which rooms, surfaces and ducts, how many samples), a trained technician network with kits and a chain-of-custody app, remote IH sign-off, a lab partner, a compliance-clock dashboard for carriers, and a 'smoke clearance certificate' for resale and escrow. Priced at a fraction of full CIH scopes.
why_now: The laws were signed two weeks ago with an effective date of Jan 1, 2027, LA County is investigating Farmers over Eaton/Palisades claim denials, a proposed class action targets vendor assessments, and carriers oppose but must comply. The gap between the compliance date and the state standard is a 2-3 year window in which the best-documented protocol becomes the de facto reference, and other fire states (Colorado, Oregon, Hawaii) are watching.
revenue_model: Per-home assessment of $1,800-$4,500 (paid by insurer under AB 1795 or the policyholder), $500 clearance-certificate add-on, lab pass-through margin, SaaS compliance dashboard for carriers at $2-$5 per claim per month, and training and certification fees for restoration technicians.
non_obvious_insight: In smoke disputes the lab is rarely the fight; the fight is the sampling design and the pass/fail threshold. Carriers whose vendors sample five spots and compare against urban background dust get 'clean' results by construction. Whoever publishes a transparent, replicable sampling grid with chain of custody writes the eventual standard, because regulators borrow the protocol with the most field data.
first_30_days: Recruit two CIHs and one toxicologist as an advisory board and draft 'Interim Smoke Assessment Protocol v0.1' for public comment. Train 6-10 IICRC-certified restoration technicians and buy sampling kits. Sell 20 pilot assessments in Altadena and Palisades at a subsidized $950 through public adjusters and attorneys, gathering data and case studies. Pitch 3 carriers and 2 TPAs on 30-day compliance capacity before January 1, offering a pilot at cost in exchange for using the protocol.

title: Closed-Loop Solvents for the Generic GLP-1 Wave
one_liner: Solvent-recovery-as-a-service for peptide CDMOs and new generic semaglutide makers, because the pill era and the April 2026 patent expiries multiply peptide API output and its solvent waste.
customer: Generic GLP-1 manufacturers ramping in India (40+ launchers), Canada, Brazil, China and Turkey, plus peptide CDMOs and US peptide onshoring projects. The buyer is the plant's operations or EHS head, who is under margin pressure.
problem: Chemically synthesized and purified peptides are among the most solvent-hungry drugs (published process-mass-intensity estimates run around 10,000 kg of waste per kg of API, versus a few hundred for small molecules). Coupling and cleavage use DMF, NMP, DCM and TFA. RP-HPLC purification burns acetonitrile. DMF and NMP face tightening worker-exposure rules, and TFA is drawing PFAS scrutiny in Europe. Oral semaglutide needs about 25 mg a day versus 2.4 mg a week for the pen, roughly 70x more API per patient-week, so tonnage and waste balloon. Lilly's orforglipron is a small molecule and avoids this, so the burden lands on Novo's supply chain and the thin-margin generics.
solution: Containerized, GMP-adjacent recovery skids (fractional distillation, membrane polishing, carbon and ion-exchange for TFA capture) leased or run on a tolling basis. Recovered DMF and acetonitrile come back with a certificate of analysis for reuse in non-final steps, and a mass-balance ledger documents the reduced hazardous waste for regulators, auditors and customers. The first product is a paid batch-level solvent mass-balance audit, which leads to tolling.
why_now: Semaglutide patents expired across India, Canada, Brazil, China and Turkey around April 2026 and dozens of makers are scaling at once. The Wegovy pill launched Jan 5, 2026 and the pill format changes API volume by an order of magnitude or more. Solvent regulation is tightening. Acetonitrile has had repeated supply shocks.
revenue_model: Per-kg-recovered tolling fees, or a monthly skid lease plus a share of avoided virgin-solvent and incineration cost (customers typically keep 30-40% savings). Add-on fees for regulatory documentation.
non_obvious_insight: The GLP-1 story is told in doses, but its physical footprint is solvent mass. The second-tier generic makers who cannot afford incineration and cannot buy virgin acetonitrile at spot prices are the ones who will pay for recovery, not Novo or Lilly.
first_30_days: Offer five generic makers or CDMOs in Hyderabad, Ahmedabad and Ontario a free solvent mass-balance audit of one batch. Partner with an existing pharma-grade solvent tolling distiller so no capex is needed. Aim for one paid 5-10 tonne tolling pilot within 90 days and use the audit data to sell skid leases.

title: Night Ledger: Sleep Evidence for Live-In Aides
one_liner: A camera-free $35 bedroom-door sensor kit that logs every night-time awakening of a dementia patient, giving live-in agencies court-grade proof of sleep or interruption, and a case for the second aide.
customer: Licensed home care agencies with 20-300 24-hour live-in cases, starting with Medicaid-contracted agencies in NYC, Long Island, Westchester and northern NJ. Secondary: families who employ live-in aides directly. Agencies pay.
problem: Live-in aides are paid for 13 of 24 hours. That is legal in New York only if the aide gets 8 hours of sleep, 5 of them uninterrupted, plus 3 hours for meals. A dementia patient who sundowns, wanders and needs toileting at 2am makes that fiction. The only evidence of sleep is the aide's own signed timesheet. Agencies face wage class actions and NYSDOL claims. Aides are underpaid and quit. The night, the most expensive and dangerous stretch of care, is the least measured.
solution: Two or three battery-powered motion or mmWave sensors (bedroom door, hallway, bathroom, exit door) and a hub that phones home. There is no video and no audio, because aides hate being watched and families in some states cannot legally record them. Each morning it produces a one-page Night Report: the longest uninterrupted stretch, the number of get-ups, exit-seeking events, and a one-tap aide confirmation of what was actually done. Quiet nights support the 13-hour pay. Noisy nights trigger a pay correction and build a documented case for the plan to authorize split-shift (two-aide) coverage. Families get 2am exit-seeking alerts on the same hardware.
why_now: In January 2026 a New York court reopened hundreds of shelved 24-hour-aide wage claims against NYSDOL and granted class certification (Legal Aid and NCLEJ). Federal DOL has only proposed reinstating the companionship exemption (July 2025). The 2013 rule is still the law, private rights of action are untouched, and state law in NY, NJ and CA applies regardless. Sensors, BLE and mmWave chips are now cheap enough to rent per case. The oldest boomers turn 80 this year, so live-in dementia cases are growing.
revenue_model: $79 per active live-in case per month, with the sensor kit rented and shipped. A one-time $1,500 to $3,000 wage-liability audit for agencies is the entry product. Families add-on at $29 per month for night alerts. Later, a fee for documentation packages that support split-shift authorization requests.
non_obvious_insight: Everyone treats the 13-hour rule as a labor-cost fight. Insiders know the same nightly record is a liability shield for the agency, proof of a heavier case that can justify two aides billed at full rate, and evidence for the aide, all at once. Nobody has built it because the buyer, the agency, has spent years preferring not to have the data. A class action changes that preference. Cameras are the wrong tool. Aides quit over them, and door-and-hallway motion data is enough.
first_30_days: Buy 40 off-the-shelf Zigbee or BLE motion sensors and a Pi or cellular hub. Write a script that emails a Night Report. Sell the audit as a service to 3 small LHCSAs in Brooklyn, Queens or Bergen County through wage-and-hour defense attorneys and home care association meetings, by offering a free 2-week pilot on their five heaviest cases. Ask two worker centers to beta test with aides and give aides their own copy of the log. The first paid pilots should come from agencies that were just sued or received a DOL inquiry.

title: Live Herd Maps for Hiking Apps
one_liner: Collar-derived herd positions pushed to hiking and mountain-bike apps so hikers reroute around cattle, funded by the destination that profits from the landscape.
customer: Alpine and mountain destination bodies, municipalities and trail associations paying for a valley licence. Secondary buyers are livestock-liability insurers and the trail apps themselves as distribution partners.
problem: Cattle-hiker incidents have produced large liability judgments in the Alps (reported in Tyrol and elsewhere), pushing farmers to fence trails or abandon high pastures, which erodes the landscape tourists come for. Hiker density is rising with overtourism. The farmer knows where the cows are, and virtual-fencing and GPS collars already record it, but the hiker does not.
solution: Ingest positions from virtual-fencing and GPS collars and cheap satellite or LoRa tags, and publish geofenced herd zones at roughly 30-minute freshness through an open API to trail apps such as Outdooractive, Komoot, AllTrails and Gaia. Add trailhead QR and SMS warnings and detour suggestions. The incident log becomes the farmer's dated proof of warnings issued, which supports liability cover and premium credits. A US variant covers guardian-dog and cattle conflicts on western grazing allotments.
why_now: Virtual-fencing collars (Halter, Nofence) have scaled from pilots to fleets, and satellite IoT now covers valleys without cell service. International arrivals hit about 1.52B in 2025, and Spain, Italy and Japan are all trying to move visitors off crowded routes. Destinations have new levies and budgets to spend on dispersal.
revenue_model: EUR12K-EUR40K/yr per valley from destination bodies. A collar-vendor or farmer data fee of EUR3-EUR6 per collar per month. Insurer data licences and app API fees.
non_obvious_insight: The herd data is a by-product already collected for a different reason, and the liability problem is fundamentally an information problem. Selling to the destination rather than the farmer solves who pays, because the destination's product is the pastoral landscape.
first_30_days: Pick one valley (Tyrol, Graubunden or Colorado) with an existing collar deployment, and sign the destination body and farmers' cooperative to a summer-2027 pilot by March. Build a GPX geofence feed and get one trail app to test it as a data partner.

title: Lead-Refund Recovery for Home-Service Pros
one_liner: Auto-dispute junk paid leads from Google Local Services, Angi, Thumbtack and Yelp, and take a share of the credits recovered.
customer: HVAC, plumbing, roofing, locksmith, garage-door, pest and electrical firms with 3-30 employees spending $2k-30k a month on paid leads.
problem: A large share of paid leads are spam, wrong-service, out-of-area or duplicates (typically cited at 20-40%; prior knowledge). Disputes are manual and deadline-bound, so owners rarely file. Getting customers is the top small-business challenge, so the spend is untouchable but the waste is fixable.
solution: Connect ad and lead accounts and the phone system's call recordings. Transcribe and classify each lead against each platform's dispute reasons, file disputes with evidence inside the window, track credits, and flag chronically junky sources. A monthly report shows net cost per real lead.
why_now: Cheap call transcription and LLM classification make per-lead review nearly free, and legacy local-marketing vendors are shrinking and raising prices, which raises the value of every recovered credit.
revenue_model: 20-25% of credits recovered (no credit, no fee), or $99/month per account.
non_obvious_insight: Nobody sells lead-refund recovery because each dispute is worth $30-150, but automation turns them into a portfolio. Recovered credits are pure margin for the owner.
first_30_days: Ask 10 contractors from local trade Facebook groups for 90 days of lead exports and call logs. File disputes manually to learn acceptance rates, then automate the top three reason codes.

title: Independent Auditor of Real Agent-Commerce Volume
one_liner: A neutral measurement firm that separates real agent payments from wash trading and testing, then sells diligence to investors and behavioral AML monitoring to the trust banks that carry the flows.
customer: Investors and acquirers diligencing agent-payment startups, protocol foundations and ecosystem funds that allocate grants on volume, OCC-chartered trust banks, stablecoin issuers and MSBs onboarding agent-wallet fintechs, and card networks and acquirers.
problem: Bloomberg found that about $24M of on-chain agent commerce shrinks to about $1.6M once self-trading wallets are removed, and Base logged about 97M protocol transactions with no one able to say how many were live. Meanwhile Tempo raised $500M and every network is announcing agent rails. KYC at onboarding does not fit wallets that act autonomously, and continuous behavioral KYC is the flagged gap.
solution: Cluster wallets, detect self-dealing, and classify each flow as test, wash or real economic activity (unique counterparties, fiat off-ramps, merchant tie-outs) across x402, MPP and AP2 settlement. Publish a free index, sell diligence reports, and offer an agent-tuned monitoring API that scores velocity, counterparty concentration and sanctions-adjacent exposure for BSA/AML programs.
why_now: x402 moved to the Linux Foundation in April 2026 and MPP is live. The Fed proposed GENIUS Act issuer rules on 2026-09-24, and OCC trust charters are being handed out (Circle on 2026-07-10, Coinbase in April, Bridge conditionally). A Senate report alleging about $2B of Iran-linked Tether flows raises the cost of weak compliance.
revenue_model: Diligence engagements at $15-60k each, monitoring subscriptions at $5-30k per month per bank or issuer, and data licensing to funds and networks.
non_obvious_insight: In a hype market the scarce good is credible measurement, and a firm with no token or protocol stake is the only party everyone can trust. The clustering work that debunks the volume numbers is the same compliance product regulated banks will have to buy, and it needs both on-chain forensics and agent-protocol fluency.
first_30_days: Two on-chain analysts build the wash filter on public data (Dune or Flipside), publish 'Real vs Reported Agent Commerce' with an open methodology, and pitch it to 15 funds and 3 foundations. Charge for the first bespoke diligence report within the month, and let the free index drive inbound.

title: Wildfire Evacuation Autopilot for Campsites and Hotels
one_liner: Satellite fire-spread alerts plus pre-contracted buses, routes and multilingual guest messaging turn every tourist lodging in fire country into an evacuation node.
customer: Campsites, holiday parks and hotels in fire-prone Mediterranean regions (France's Aude, Var and Gironde, Catalonia, Greece, Portugal, Croatia), plus regional tourism boards and insurers.
problem: Summer wildfires now force sudden evacuations of thousands of tourists who have no local knowledge, often no cars and no shared language. Duty of care sits with small operators holding paper plans they have never drilled, while insurers tighten terms.
solution: A site-specific evacuation plan with two routes and a refuge, ingestion of hourly fire detections (NASA FIRMS, Copernicus EFFIS and commercial satellite feeds), wind-aware fire arrival estimates per site, and automatic guest alerts by WhatsApp or SMS in the guest's language using check-in data. It includes a staff checklist and drills, and standby contracts with local coach operators.
why_now: Higher-frequency satellite fire detection arrived with early-2025 launches such as FireSat, and wildfire seasons in 2025 were severe across Southern Europe. Insurers and regulators are pressing small operators.
revenue_model: EUR 300-1,200 per site per year, margin on coach standby retainers, insurer premium-discount share and regional government contracts.
non_obvious_insight: Tourist lodging is the largest concentration of people in fire zones with no local knowledge, no vehicles and no common language, and the legal duty sits with operators who cannot afford risk consultants.
first_30_days: Recruit 25 campsites in Aude, Hérault, Var and Gironde through the camping federation. Deliver a plan PDF and WhatsApp alerts at EUR 390 per year, run one drill and pitch two insurers with results.

title: Circle Cue: Name Whispers for Early Dementia
one_liner: Consent-only Bluetooth badges let earbuds whisper who a person is and one line of context to someone with mild cognitive impairment, with no cameras and no face recognition.
customer: Families of people with mild cognitive impairment or early Alzheimer's ($149 kit plus $15 a month), memory cafes, senior centers and faith groups, and later Medicare Advantage plans and dementia-care programs.
problem: People in early dementia often withdraw because forgetting names is humiliating, and caregivers watch the social world shrink. Face-recognition glasses are legally and ethically fraught (biometric-privacy laws), and dementia technology focuses on safety tracking rather than social participation.
solution: Circle members (family, neighbors, club regulars) opt in by wearing small Bluetooth badges with rotating IDs. The user's phone detects nearby IDs and whispers, for example, 'Tom Reyes, your neighbor; knee surgery last month' from a one-line card written by the circle and managed by the caregiver. It works offline and cards expire to avoid stale information.
why_now: Cheap BLE, on-device speech and summarization, and LE Audio earbuds make this cheap to build. FDA-cleared Alzheimer's blood tests (2025) and anti-amyloid drugs are pushing diagnosis earlier, creating a fast-growing population that is cognitively capable and socially at risk for years.
revenue_model: Hardware kit, monthly subscription, and B2B circle licenses for memory cafes and senior centers. Later: plan-funded coverage.
non_obvious_insight: The privacy-safe alternative to face recognition is consent by badge: a small, fully opt-in social graph of 10-30 people that covers most of what the person meets each week. Consent is the feature, and it turns surveillance tech into hospitality.
first_30_days: Partner with three memory cafes. Make 30 badges (about $4 each) and a prototype app. Trial with five families free, measure outings per week before and after, then sell $149 kits.

title: Fitness-Adjusted Longevity Reports for Retirement Advisors
one_liner: A report that turns a client's own wearable and clinic metrics (VO2max, resting heart rate, grip strength, gait speed, sleep) into a life-expectancy range for Social Security claiming, annuity timing and withdrawal-rate decisions, sold to fee-only advisors.
customer: Fee-only RIAs and retirement planners serving affluent pre-retirees aged 58-70, at $75-150 per client report or $300-600 a month per advisor. Later customers are planning-software vendors and annuity carriers.
problem: Social Security is the largest lifetime asset most households own. Claiming at 70 instead of 62 raises the monthly benefit by roughly three-quarters, and the break-even sits around 80-83. That decision hinges on life expectancy, but planners use population tables. Clients in the top fitness quintile can plausibly outlive the average by several years, and the sedentary can be the opposite. Early claiming reportedly jumped in 2025 amid trust-fund and SSA-staffing fears, so many people are choosing blind.
solution: Adjust standard actuarial tables using published hazard ratios for cardiorespiratory fitness, gait speed, grip strength and resting-heart-rate trends. Output a range, not a point estimate, showing break-even age versus the chance of reaching it. Data comes in by consented export from Apple Health, Garmin or Oura and is processed locally. The PDF carries methodology and disclaimers written for advisor compliance, and it is explicitly not medical advice or insurance underwriting.
why_now: Consumer wearables now deliver near-clinical metrics, including FDA-cleared hypertension notifications on Apple Watch in 2025 and VO2max estimates on most premium devices. Basic planning software is being commoditized by AI, so advisors need differentiated inputs. A wave of early Social Security claiming in 2025 shows clients are making irreversible choices under fear. Advisors have avoided health data because of privacy concerns, but client-owned wearable data solves the consent problem.
revenue_model: Per-report pricing of $75-150, advisor subscriptions of $300-600 a month, and later white-label integrations with planning tools. Annuity carriers may pay for qualified leads.
non_obvious_insight: Planners have been told for decades to plan for longevity risk while seeing only age and sex, and wearables have quietly built the best individual mortality signal outside a hospital. A plus or minus 4-year shift is enough to move the claiming break-even, so precision is not needed. The buyer is the advisor, who needs a fiduciary-safe way to bring health into the conversation.
first_30_days: Build the calculator from published cohort studies on fitness and gait speed and a standard actuarial table, and have a consulting actuary review it for $3-5k. Run 30 free reports for eight advisors in fitness-forward niches such as physician-focused planners and FIRE planners. Collect feedback and objections. Then charge $99 a report, with no health data stored on your servers.

title: Sponsor-Paid Care Network for Canine Trials
one_liner: Biotechs pay for dogs' cancer care in exchange for clean, immune-competent efficacy data, solving pet-owner affordability and drug-developer validation at once.
customer: Clinical-stage biotechs (including AI-drug-discovery companies) and animal-health developers that need cheap in vivo efficacy and safety signals pay per enrolled dog. General-practice and specialty clinics are site partners. Foundations can co-fund.
problem: 85% of vet professionals say clients decline care at estimates of $1,000 or less, and about 80% of dogs with lymphoma never receive IV chemo. On the other side, AI-designed drugs are bottlenecked by assays and validation, mouse models predict poorly, and FDA's Sept 21, 2026 rule makes sponsors show that non-animal methods are 'adequately validated'. Spontaneous tumors in pet dogs (lymphoma, osteosarcoma, mast cell, bladder cancer) are well-established human-relevant models, yet trials struggle to recruit because the dogs are first seen in general practices.
solution: A network of 30-60 general practices plus a few specialty centers. AI trial-matching runs over practice-management data and an owner-facing trial finder. Sponsors fund a standard-of-care baseline (diagnostics and supportive care) so owners get treatment free. The studio handles owner consent, GCP-style data capture, INAD/CVM paperwork, and opt-in blood and tissue banking. Start with observational registries and PK/PD window studies of oral and repurposed generic drugs, then move to sponsor-funded interventional studies.
why_now: AI-biotech funding is over $6B in 2026 and sponsors are hunting for validation evidence. FDA's Sept 2026 rule and its 25-use-case NAM database push developers away from lab animals without banning them. Duffield ($250M) and PetSmart Charities are funding 'access to care', so grant co-funding for clinics is available. Oral options like Laverdia now make community-level oncology treatable.
revenue_model: $15-30k per enrolled dog (treatment, site fees, monitoring, data), at roughly 30% gross margin. $100-250k per observational registry or PK window study. Foundation grants subsidize owner-side costs.
non_obvious_insight: Pet trials fail on recruitment and owner cost, not on science. The general-practice vet is where 90% of cases first appear, and no one connects them to sponsors. Turning a sponsor's development budget into owners' treatment budgets solves the affordability crisis and delivers a data product for drug developers.
first_30_days: Recruit 5 clinics and one board-certified oncologist as scientific lead. Pitch 10 biotechs on a $100-200k canine lymphoma real-world-outcomes registry or a dog PK window study of a repurposed oral drug. Co-apply for a foundation grant to cover owner costs. Keep the first studies observational or extra-label to stay clear of the heavier INAD requirements. First revenue in about 4-6 months.

title: Tip Passport: Mortgage-Ready Records for Tipped Workers
one_liner: An app that logs every cash and card tip in a lender-grade ledger so young bartenders, stylists, servers and valets can claim the new tip deduction and finally qualify for a mortgage or lease.
customer: Gen Z and young-millennial tipped workers (servers, bartenders, hair and nail techs, barbers, delivery and other occupations on the IRS list) earning $50-$120k with largely undocumented cash tips. Lenders and landlords pay for verified income.
problem: Cash tips have long been under-reported to avoid tax, so returns show low income and lenders qualify people on returns and W-2s. A stylist netting $90k cannot get a mortgage. The new deduction of up to $25,000 in qualified tips makes reporting valuable, but workers have no system, fear audits, and employer POS captures only card tips.
solution: One-tap, voice and QR tip logging with imports from Venmo, Cash App and POS. It produces monthly tip statements in IRS-recognized format, a deduction-ready schedule, a tax-reserve estimate and a 'lender pack' with 24-month income narrative reconciled to bank deposits. The pack is accepted by partner bank-statement lenders and landlords. Built-in classification excludes service charges and mandatory gratuities that do not qualify.
why_now: Final regulations (TD 10044) published April 13, 2026 confirm the 70+ qualifying occupations for the deduction on tips received in 2025-2028. 2026 is the first year workers can plan around it. The sunset after 2028 creates a roughly two-year window to build the 24-month record lenders want, and non-QM bank-statement lending is available.
revenue_model: $8-$12 per month or $79 per year, a lender referral fee of $300-$1,500 per funded loan, $25 per landlord verification report, and a B2B retention perk sold to salon suites and restaurant groups.
non_obvious_insight: A tax incentive flips the incentive from hiding income to documenting it for the first time in decades, and the same document (proof of income) is worth ten times the tax savings because it unlocks a mortgage. The moat is trusted, lender-accepted record-keeping, not tax prep.
first_30_days: Find 100 stylists and bartenders through salon-suite communities and beauty and hospitality creators on social media. Sell a tip ledger plus deduction estimate at $9 per month. Partner with one bank-statement lender and one CPA who signs off on the statement format. Track pre-approvals within 90 days as the proof point.

title: Hospital-Guaranteed Loans for Excluded Health Programs
one_liner: Employer-cosigned, service-obligation tuition loans for nursing, OT, PT and counseling students that the new federal caps abandoned.
customer: Hospital systems, rural health networks, behavioral-health agencies and skilled-nursing chains (they guarantee or buy down); their incoming students and employees; a CDFI or specialty-finance fund as capital partner.
problem: Since July 1, 2026 Grad PLUS is gone, grad loans are capped at $20.5k per year and $100k total, and nursing, OT, PT, counseling, psychology and social work were excluded from the higher 'professional' cap. Private lenders are tightening, and predatory loans run up to 16% APR. These fields face the most AI-resistant shortages, including nurse educators, NPs and therapists.
solution: A loan product with employer guarantee or interest buy-down, a 2-3 year service commitment, and retention-linked forgiveness paid by the employer as tenure accrues. Underwrite on licensure pass rates and a signed job offer rather than FICO. The employer gets a cheaper pipeline and retention tool than agency staffing or sign-on bonuses.
why_now: The cap regime took effect in July 2026. A healthcare-association lawsuit is pending, with a December 2026 suspension deadline, so uncertainty is high. Incumbent lenders are retreating. Hospitals are under labor-cost pressure.
revenue_model: 2-3% origination fee, servicing spread, and a per-participant employer program fee. Use a bank-partner or licensed-lender model at first so you don't need your own lending licenses.
non_obvious_insight: Insiders read the cap as proof these programs are too risky to finance. In fact, licensure-gated wages and very high employment make them among the best credits in higher ed. The natural underwriter is not a bank but the employer who would otherwise pay a large premium for temporary staff.
first_30_days: Pick one state and 2 hospital systems that already run tuition assistance. Pitch a $2M pilot warehouse line from a CDFI or hospital foundation for about 20 students starting January 2027. Engage a licensed bank or lender partner and counsel on structure.

title: Street-Level Gas Pipe Retirement Optimizer
one_liner: Software plus a turnkey block-by-block electrification crew that tells gas utilities which streets to retire instead of replace.
customer: Regulated gas distribution utilities in MA, NY, CO, MN, WA, CA and IL, and their regulators. Funding comes from pipe-replacement capex budgets.
problem: Electrification shrinks gas throughput, so fixed pipe costs land on fewer customers. Utilities still replace leak-prone mains at millions of dollars per mile. Regulators (for example Massachusetts DPU 20-80-B) demand non-pipeline alternatives, but nobody optimizes at street-segment level. Heat pump quotes run ~$9,000 and labor is scarce.
solution: GIS, billing and housing-stock analytics that score each pipe segment for retire-versus-replace, and find streets where electrifying 30-80 homes costs less than replacing the main. Then deliver the electrification block by block: group purchase, one crew per street per week, optionally networked geothermal. It is filed as a utility non-pipeline alternative.
why_now: State non-pipeline-alternative orders and thermal-energy-network laws are in force. With federal credits dead, utility-funded programs are the only scaled electrification channel. Ratepayer affordability pressure makes stranded pipe a live issue.
revenue_model: $250-500k a year SaaS per utility plus a per-home program fee ($5-12k) paid from avoided pipe capex.
non_obvious_insight: Gas utilities' problem is no longer selling heat pumps. It is stranded pipe. Their pipe replacement capex is the electrification budget hiding in plain sight.
first_30_days: Model one Massachusetts or New York utility territory from public leak-prone-pipe, assessor and census data. Publish a 'retire-first streets' list for one city. Pitch a city sustainability office, a regulator and two utility strategy VPs. Sell a $60-100k pilot analysis.

title: Infection-Safe Energy Retrofits for Animal Shelters
one_liner: A shared-savings energy contractor that designs heat-recovery ventilation, heat pumps and batteries around shelter-medicine infection-control rules, funded by pet-welfare philanthropy and paid partly by utility resilience programs.
customer: Animal shelters, humane societies, boarding and daycare facilities and 24-hour emergency vet hospitals. Funders include pet-welfare foundations and utilities. The buyer is the shelter director or board, and the payers are philanthropy plus shared savings.
problem: Shelters must move a lot of conditioned air (guidelines commonly call for roughly 10-20 air changes per hour) to control respiratory disease, run heavy laundry and hot-water loads 24/7, and cannot go dark in a heat wave or outage. Utility rates rose 7.3% in a year. Most are nonprofits in old buildings, and energy contractors either cut ventilation (raising disease risk) or refuse the job. Meanwhile pet philanthropy is arriving but is aimed at care, not capex (Duffield's $250M over 5 years starts with 250 x $10K grants).
solution: A standard package built around air-change and zoning constraints: energy-recovery ventilation, heat pump water heaters for laundry, right-sized battery and optional solar with a critical-load panel. It is financed by grants, utility rebates, elective-pay tax credits where still eligible (to be verified per project) and shared savings. Shelters also commit to serve as pet-inclusive cooling or warming refuge in emergencies, with a utility or city paying an availability fee.
why_now: Duffield's $250M commitment (September 17, 2026) and PetSmart Charities' $100M pledge put unprecedented money into shelters. Electricity prices, storage costs (about $70/kWh packs) and utility resilience programs make small batteries viable, and no vendor has encoded shelter-medicine ventilation rules.
revenue_model: Design and project-management fee of 8-12% on $60-250K retrofits, plus a 20-30% share of verified savings for 7-10 years on projects financed by grant or green-loan capital, plus utility or city availability payments for refuge capacity.
non_obvious_insight: The binding constraint in a shelter is infection control, not kWh. The first vendor that treats ventilation and cross-contamination as design rules owns a trusted niche, and philanthropy has cash but no capex vehicle for energy.
first_30_days: Offer 10 shelters free utility-bill audits and publish an anonymized shelter energy benchmark. Help 3 of them use first-round philanthropic grants to fund detailed audits. Close one small paid project (heat pump water heaters for laundry) to build a case study. Talk to two utilities about a refuge availability payment.

title: Child-in-the-Room Detector for Voice AI
one_liner: A tiny on-device SDK that infers from a few seconds of speech whether a speaker is likely a child, so voice assistants, cars, TVs and toys can drop into a safe policy tier without any login, camera or ID.
customer: OEMs of smart speakers, TVs and in-car assistants, voice-AI and companion app makers, and toy makers.
problem: Ambient voice AI serves shared households with no account or age signal. Laws and probes (CA SB 243, the FTC 6(b) inquiry, COPPA 'actual knowledge') create duties once a minor is present. Devices cannot tell a child from an adult, and asking kids to log in fails. The amended COPPA rule's biometric coverage makes storing voiceprints risky.
solution: An SDK under 5MB that classifies speaker age band (under 9, 9-15, adult) with calibrated confidence and an abstain option, using ephemeral features and never storing voiceprints. It returns a 'minor-likely' signal to trigger safe modes (topic limits, no romance roleplay, safe-messaging protocols) with audit logs. It is benchmarked publicly across accents and speech differences and fails safe by default.
why_now: Lawsuits and the FTC inquiry are pushing platforms to prove they detect minors, on-device speech encoders are good enough, and the brief flags a demand for privacy-preserving, non-ID age signals.
revenue_model: Per-device royalty of $0.10-0.50 or per-MAU pricing, plus paid integration and benchmark-certification services.
non_obvious_insight: For a voice product, the best age signal is the voice itself, with no ID, camera or login. The error costs are asymmetric: treating an adult as a child is cheap, the reverse is not, so 'fail safe' is the sales pitch.
first_30_days: Fine-tune an open speech encoder on licensed or consented child and adult speech corpora. Publish an open benchmark and baseline. Talk to 10 voice-AI and toy builders. Land 2 paid pilots at $3-5k each.

title: Robot Basecoating for Tabletop Miniature Armies
one_liner: A batch service where vision-guided robot airbrush cells prime, zenithal-shade and basecoat plastic miniatures so hobbyists only paint the details.
customer: Tabletop wargamers with unpainted backlogs, tournament players who need painted armies, and commission-painter studios who subcontract the tedious stages.
problem: An army is 100+ models, and priming and basecoating are the tedious first 60% of the work. Commission painters charge $10-60 per model and take months. Games Workshop's FY2026 revenue of GBP 626.8M shows the scale of the hobby.
solution: Customers ship assembled models. A low-cost robot arm learned from expert airbrushers primes, zenithal-shades and single-color basecoats. Humans QA and finish edges, and the army returns in about 10 days. Start human-in-the-loop with teleoperation and automate progressively.
why_now: Low-cost open-source robot arms and imitation-learning policies matured in 2025. A search for a commercial robot-airbrush painting service for miniatures found none.
revenue_model: $1.50-4 per model, $99-399 per army, and a subscription 'paint club' for batches.
non_obvious_insight: The community fetishizes painting but dislikes the first stage. The robot needs consistency, not artistry, on surfaces that hidden under detail work. Human painters keep the premium layer and become customers and distribution.
first_30_days: Hand-airbrush 50 armies to validate price and turnaround through r/Warhammer and local clubs. Build a teleop rig with a ~$3k arm and airbrush. Ship the first 20 orders.

title: Court-Ready Smoke Testing Protocol for Fire Survivors
one_liner: A standardized smoke and ash sampling protocol plus lab network that satisfies California's new smoke-damage presumption law, sold to public adjusters, policyholders and eventually carriers.
customer: Public adjusters, policyholder attorneys and restoration contractors handling open LA and Southern California fire claims, paying $1,200-3,500 per home. Carriers and TPAs are a later channel, since the law makes testing an insurer-funded cost.
problem: Fire survivors have fought carriers for months or years over whether smoke-contaminated homes are safe. There is no agreed testing or restoration standard, so each claim becomes a fight between competing consultants. The new law shifts testing cost to insurers and blocks Additional Living Expense from ending until homes are restored and safe.
solution: A published sampling protocol and chain-of-custody workflow run by certified industrial hygienists and partner labs. It produces a report format mapped to the statute's language (presumption, testing funded by insurers, pre-loss restoration). We bundle software that generates the sampling plan, tracks lab results, and drafts the repair scope. Sell to public adjusters first, then offer carriers a neutral-standard option.
why_now: AB 1795 was signed on 2026-09-15 and introduces a smoke-damage presumption, insurer-paid testing and sampling, inspection and claims-handling timelines, and adjuster training. The industry group APCIA asked that guidance be 'grounded in credible science, valid methodologies.' SB 876, signed 2026-09-28 and effective 2027-01-01, doubles penalties for unfair claims practices during declared emergencies and requires insurers to file disaster recovery plans, raising the stakes on slow claims.
revenue_model: Per-home testing and reporting fee of $1,200-3,500. Software seats for public adjusters at $200-400 per month. Later a per-claim neutral-testing fee from carriers and TPAs, and lab partnership revenue share.
non_obvious_insight: The law creates a paid testing mandate without naming a standard, so whoever defines the accepted protocol captures the spend. Evidence: https://www.insurancejournal.com/news/west/2026/09/15/885209.htm (presumption, insurer-paid testing, ALE protections; APCIA's 'credible science' quote; contentious smoke claims after the 2025 LA fires) and https://www.insurance.ca.gov/0400-news/0100-press-releases/release031-2026.cfm (Commissioner Lara: families 'have spent months, and sometimes years, fighting over whether their homes were safe'). https://www.insurance.ca.gov/0400-news/0100-press-releases/2026/release034-2026.cfm covers SB 876, including doubled penalties in emergencies and a 15-day adjuster-change update. Public adjusters have no neutral, repeatable science kit today, and carriers lose in disputes when their own hired consultant is the only standard.
first_30_days: Partner with 2 certified industrial hygienists and 1 accredited lab in the LA area. Draft the protocol from published standards and the statute text. Offer 10 public adjusters with open Eaton and Palisades claims a discounted first three homes in exchange for case studies. Invite APCIA member claim managers to review the protocol for credibility.

title: Remote Athletic Trainer Coverage for Rural Schools
one_liner: A subscription sideline triage line, protocol library and documentation service that stretches one licensed athletic trainer across many schools.
customer: Rural and small school districts, state athletic associations and school risk pools paying $6-20k per school per season.
problem: NATA-cited figures show about 41 percent of Kansas schools and 68 percent of Oklahoma schools lack an athletic trainer, only about a third of Arkansas schools have one, and Massachusetts does not require one (Boston Globe, September 28, 2026). Coaches make return-to-play calls and handle concussions, heat and cardiac emergencies ad hoc, and districts carry the liability.
solution: Licensed ATs run a game-time line where coaches call or video-chat for triage; ATs guide return-to-play, do next-day follow-ups, document per state concussion law, and supply emergency action plans and coach training. Optional phase two: AT review of clips from schools' existing AI cameras.
why_now: 2026 shortage coverage keeps escalating, legislatures are debating mandates, and schools already own cheap AI cameras and video-call tools.
revenue_model: $6-20k per school per season, district-wide contracts, risk-pool discounts, and per-event tournament coverage fees.
non_obvious_insight: Training more ATs will not fix this within five years; extending each AT's reach 5-10x will. School insurers and risk pools care about concussion litigation and will subsidize it, so it is sold as liability reduction rather than healthcare.
first_30_days: Recruit 5 part-time or retired ATs licensed in one state, pitch 10 districts on a 4-week football-season pilot at $2.5k, and pitch that state's school risk pool on co-funding.

title: Paid Caregiver Demonstration-Data Cooperative
one_liner: Home-care aides and family caregivers wear head cameras during non-intimate care tasks and earn revenue share from licensing that data to robot-foundation-model companies.
customer: Robotics labs and humanoid makers buying home-task demonstration data (Figure, 1X, Skild, Physical Intelligence, Generalist-class buyers), at $60-150 per usable hour. Home-care agencies are the distribution partner.
problem: Humanoid progress is bottlenecked on physical-world data. Data vendors already pay people to film themselves making coffee (XDOF about $50M annualized, Mecka projecting $100M ARR). Nobody has data on the hardest, highest-value home tasks: walker and transfer assistance, modified-diet meal prep, laundry and tidying around frail people. Meanwhile aides earn under $35k and agencies see 77-80% turnover.
solution: Give each aide a $150 camera kit and an on-device consent and blurring pipeline. Capture only task categories that avoid intimate care, with care-recipient or proxy consent per home. Pay a per-hour data premium on top of wages, which agencies use as a retention bonus, and sell curated, labeled datasets.
why_now: Robot data-as-a-service went from nothing to unicorn valuations in months (Sep 2026). Immigration crackdowns are draining the care workforce, so agencies are desperate for retention tools that do not raise Medicaid-capped rates.
revenue_model: License datasets at $60-150 per hour. Pay workers 30-40%, agency 10% and keep the remainder. Add curation and labeling fees.
non_obvious_insight: Robots cannot yet enter the homes that hold the training data they most need, but the lowest-paid workforce in America is already inside them. Data pay solves agencies' turnover problem at no cost to a squeezed Medicaid budget.
first_30_days: Sign one home-care agency and 20 aides for a pilot. Write a consent and privacy protocol with an elder-law attorney. Pre-sell a 500-hour dataset to one robotics lab using a sample of kitchen and laundry tasks.

title: Parking-Slot Gates for Overrun Villages
one_liner: Sell tiny hotspot villages and trailheads a plate-recognition parking and coach-slot reservation system whose price rises until arrivals fit a hard cap.
customer: Municipalities, mountain and coastal park authorities and private lot operators in places like Alpine lake villages, Dolomites passes, Cinque Terre-type towns and Croatian or Greek islands. Budgets are under EUR 50K, and they already own parking revenue.
problem: Venice's day-tripper fee reportedly did not cut numbers, because a small flat fee is dwarfed by trip cost. Open villages cannot install turnstiles, but almost every day visitor arrives by car, coach or shuttle. Those arrival modes are countable and enforceable, and nobody prices them dynamically.
solution: A cheap camera and plate-recognition kit plus a web app. Visitors reserve parking and coach slots at prices that rise with demand until the cap holds. Residents and overnight guests are exempt through a plate allow-list synced from hotels' check-in data. The cap becomes a subsidy for staying overnight.
why_now: Edge computer vision and plate recognition are now cheap. Record arrivals (1.52B international in 2025) and visible failures of flat fees have made mayors ready to try hard caps. Mount Fuji's 4,000/day cap plus fee shows caps are politically acceptable, and a few Alpine lakes already require reserved road access in peak season.
revenue_model: SaaS of EUR 300-900 per month per site, plus 3-5% of slot fees collected, plus a hardware lease.
non_obvious_insight: Price the arrival mode rather than the person. Cars and coaches are the physical valve for day-trip load, and exempting overnight guests turns a congestion rule into a booking incentive that local hotels will help sell.
first_30_days: Pick 3 villages that already have paid lots. Run a manual pilot with a reservation page and a phone-camera plate check by a local attendant, with no hardware. Sign private lot operators first, since they can decide fastest. Ask mayors for a summer 2027 pilot and a letter of support.

title: Cryo-Vault for Artisan Food Microbial Cultures
one_liner: Backup-and-rescue service that fingerprints, isolates and cryo-banks the living house cultures (cheese rind flora, koji, kombucha SCOBYs, sourdough starters, mushroom spawn, natural-wine yeast) of small food producers in split-geography -80 storage, with a 48-hour emergency revival.
customer: Small artisan producers: raw-milk and farmstead cheesemakers, koji, miso and sake makers, kombucha brewers, specialty mushroom growers, sourdough bakeries, natural winemakers and cideries. Pay $250-400 intake plus $20-40/month per culture, and $400-600 per emergency rescue.
problem: A small producer's house culture is their product identity, yet it lives on the counter or in a single fridge, propagated by serial subculture. Mother cultures senesce and drift, contaminate, or get wiped out by phage (dairy) or Trichoderma-type molds (mushrooms). One crash can end a brand for months. Big culture houses won't bank a small producer's strains, and commercial biobank services are priced and designed for pharma.
solution: A mail-in kit: send a gram of culture, get back an ITS/16S-based composition fingerprint, viability and purity report, and isolated key strains. Each is banked as glycerol stocks in triplicate at two separate sites, with a dashboard of banked cultures. The rescue tier revives a viable working culture in 48 hours with contamination diagnosis, and later adds a periodic 'drift check' compared against the banked baseline. Optional fingerprint certificates for craft-authenticity claims and geographic-indication programs.
why_now: Fermentation and koji-based craft food is booming, and sequencing costs are trivial (about $30 per amplicon sample). Consolidation and climate stress are raising the cost of a culture crash. Small food makers increasingly market on 'living' and heritage claims that they can't currently back up. Laid-off microbiologists can staff this cheaply.
revenue_model: Intake fee plus recurring monthly vault subscription per culture. Per-event rescue fees. Fingerprint certificates and drift-check add-ons. Later B2B with food-safety consultants and craft trade associations, which bundle it as a member benefit.
non_obvious_insight: Cryo-banking with a genetic fingerprint is routine bench hygiene for any wet-lab, but the food world has never been offered it at a price small producers can pay. Nobody thinks of 'my sourdough' as a strain to back up until it crashes. The wedge is not the science, it is the packaging as insurance and the rescue promise.
first_30_days: Bank 10 cultures for free from friendly producers (cheesemakers, kombucha and mushroom growers) recruited through guild forums and Facebook groups. Rent -80 space at a university core, a co-lab or a local biobank. Use a commercial amplicon sequencing service for fingerprints. Publish one story about a rescued culture. Convert the first cohort to $99/month founding-member pricing. Stay strictly with BSL-1 food-grade organisms and set clear policies on pathogen refusal and shipping.

title: Satellite-Armed Sprinklers With Insurer-Grade Uptime Logs
one_liner: A satellite-backed controller that lets a homeowner arm, pre-wet and prove the working state of exterior ember sprinklers after the cell tower and power are gone.
customer: Exurban owners in Colorado foothills and Sierra or Northern California with private water tanks, pumps and exterior sprinkler systems. Installers are the channel, and regional insurers or MGAs that offer mitigation credits are the second payer.
problem: Wildfire defence fails at the exact moment cell towers burn and power drops, and app-based remote activation depends on cellular. Mitigation credits are unclaimable in practice because owners cannot document that a system was armed and working ('1,000 bucks towards a $75,000 metal roof'), and the retrofit baseline is already $8K-$25K.
solution: A $400-$600 controller sits between the pump, valve and battery. It uses LTE-M as primary and NB-NTN satellite as fallback (Skylo or Iridium NTN Direct), sending a daily signed heartbeat of tank level, pump power, valve state and battery in about 50 bytes. The owner can arm or pre-wet by satellite message from an evacuation route, and fire-hotspot feeds (VIIRS, plus FireSat data as it opens up) trigger arm prompts. The signed uptime log exports as documented mitigation for insurer credits and appeals.
why_now: NB-NTN-capable cellular IoT chips (for example Nordic's nRF9151) are shipping, and Iridium NTN Direct launches in 2026, so a satellite fallback is now a chip option rather than a custom radio. Colorado HB25-1182 has required insurers to credit documented mitigation and offer appeals since July 1, 2026. FireSat's first three operational satellites reached orbit in July 2026. Roughly 1-2 kbps satellite links are enough for a 50-byte payload.
revenue_model: $499 hardware plus $19/month service. A 15% referral fee to installers on attach sales. A per-home-per-year data fee of about $25-$50 from insurers or MGAs that accept the log as verified mitigation.
non_obvious_insight: The insurance value is not the sprinkler. It is credible evidence that the sprinkler was armed and worked, and only a device whose telemetry travels on an independent path is believable when everything terrestrial is down. Bandwidth is almost irrelevant, so this is a sub-$5/month satellite bill rather than a broadband product.
first_30_days: Buy 20 NB-NTN dev kits with a Skylo plan and wire them to pump controllers. Sign one Front Range or Sierra sprinkler installer with about 50 existing customers, and put the log format in front of one regional insurer's mitigation-credit desk to test whether it counts. Sell 10 pilot units at $299, and fall back to selling on function alone if no insurer credits it yet.

title: Consumer-Side Debt Negotiation Agent for Brazil
one_liner: A WhatsApp agent that reads a household's Open Finance data and negotiates all its debts on the debtor's behalf.
customer: Over-indebted Brazilian households, paying a success fee.
problem: Household debt is around 82% by the cited indicator, delinquency is at a record, and Lula's Sep 25 relief may reach under 1% of defaults. People face many creditors and rarely know discounts are available.
solution: With consent, pull debts from Open Finance, build a repayment plan, negotiate through lender collection channels and debt portals, and set up Pix Automatico debits. The wedge is revolving card debt and overdraft for low-income users.
why_now: Open Finance and Pix Automatico are mature and LLM agents can now negotiate reliably. The online betting ban leaves ex-bettors with debts and no plan.
revenue_model: 10-15% of the discount obtained, charged only on success.
non_obvious_insight: Existing collections platforms are lender-paid and optimise recovery. A debtor-side agent exposes rate arbitrage and gives lenders a rational counterparty at scale.
first_30_days: Run a concierge pilot with 100 users, using humans plus AI drafting, to learn discount rates by lender. Check consumer-protection rules first.
